requirements.R1: An inbound web-form lead gets a personalised email reply within two minutes
requirements.R2: Each lead gets a score from 0 to 100 computed from weights in a config file
requirements.R3: Leads above the threshold are pushed to HubSpot; the rest go to a review sheet
requirements.R4: The reply never states a price that is not in the price list
requirements.R5: A failed send or push is retried and then alerted, never dropped

kpis.name: Reply quality on simulated leads
kpis.target: >= 85% of scenarios at or above the rubric pass mark

kpis.name: Price-rule violations
kpis.how: pnpm eval counts replies with a price outside the list

kpis.name: Cost per lead
kpis.how: pnpm eval prices recorded token usage

kpis.name: Lead-to-meeting rate
kpis.how: events lead.replied and meeting.booked in the dashboard

steps.title: Contracts: lead, score, reply and connector interfaces
steps.why: Design decisions that no command can verify, so the strongest model; high is enough for a system this small, and it is reviewed because nothing else checks it.

steps.title: Scaffold repository, verify command, CI and CLAUDE.md
steps.why: Fully determined by the architecture's layout section, so the cheapest model builds it; reviewed because every later step is judged by the verify command it creates.

steps.title: Evaluation harness: simulated leads, rubric, kpi.json
steps.why: The rubric decides what 'good' means for K1 to K3, so it needs judgment, but the contract is fixed by S01.

steps.title: Scoring tests from the spec (tests only)
steps.why: Writing the expected scores is the judgment; the implementation in S05 then only has to satisfy them.

steps.title: Scoring implementation against the S04 tests
steps.why: Precise contract, and the S04 tests are frozen for this step, so a cheap model is safe and no review is needed.

steps.title: Reply engine: prompt, price-list guard, mock and live model client
steps.why: The prompt and the guard decide K1 and K2 and are judged by an evaluation, not by unit tests; high is enough because S01 fixed the interfaces.

steps.title: HubSpot connector (the exemplar) and CONNECTORS.md pattern
steps.why: First vendor integration sets the pattern for retries and idempotency.

steps.title: Review-sheet connector, following the exemplar
steps.why: Same shape as S07 with the pattern written down; contract tests prove it.

steps.title: Integrate: form webhook to reply to routing, end to end
steps.why: Seams between four components; needs judgment across the whole flow.

steps.title: Optimize reply quality and cost against K1 to K3
steps.why: Diagnosing why replies fail a rubric is judgment work; the loop is long, so it stays at high.

steps.title: Threat model and fixes: injection through lead text, webhook spoofing, secrets
steps.why: Finding what is missing is judgment; the system is small, so high suffices.

steps.title: Acceptance: final KPI readings, launch checklist, build report
steps.why: Runs and reports; no design left.
